notes:
REMEDIATION (round 4): Zainab's round-4 review (evidence/features/bio-int-003/codex/SECURITY-REVIEW-ZAINAB-ROUND4.md) confirmed round 3's IRolePermissionGateway fix correct for every ordinary role, then FAILed commit 93a0241 on ONE new finding:

ZB-INT003-07 (High): round 3 mirrored RoleType.SuperAdmin's own BIO-IDN-006 domain invariant ('never needs or has an explicit grant record') into RolePermissionGatewayAdapter - correct for a HUMAN role assignment under RoleAssignmentService's own tightly-gated endpoint, but unsafe for a service account: any actor holding only the narrow ManagePermission could mint a SuperAdmin-scoped token that auto-passed every current and future domain-permission check with no tenant grant ever consulted - a blanket tenant-admin token for integrations, which the API architecture's own rule explicitly forbids. The round-3 real-HTTP ALLOW proof relied on exactly this shortcut (it was the only production-real way to pass a permission check without a seeding capability this project lacks).

Fixed at the root, not after the fact: KnownRoles.WireFormats no longer includes SuperAdmin (ten roles remain), so IsKnown rejects it at service-account creation time before a token can ever be issued - not merely constrained once issued. RolePermissionGatewayAdapter's own now-unreachable SuperAdmin short-circuit was removed too, rather than left as dead code implying the adapter still honors that case. BIO-IDN-006's own catalogue and RoleAssignmentService are unchanged - a human can still be assigned SuperAdmin; only this project's own closed OAuth2-scope vocabulary excludes it.

Four existing tests that relied on SuperAdmin's free pass were re-pointed to real, already-valid scopes or new assertions (ServiceAccountServiceTests.cs's FakeRolePermissionGateway and one scope-literal test; ApiSecurityEndpointsTests.cs's ZB02/ZB03 seeded scopes and the AC03 whoami test, renamed to prove a well-formed token reaches real authorization distinctly from signature validation). Two new tests prove the root fix (Creating_an_account_rejects_SuperAdmin_as_a_scope, A_service_account_manager_cannot_mint_a_token_for_a_permission_they_were_never_authorised_to_delegate) plus one new real-HTTP test (ZB07_SuperAdmin_is_rejected_as_a_service_account_scope_at_the_real_http_layer, expects 400 unknown_scope).

Consequence, disclosed rather than worked around: removing the shortcut also removes the only production-real way this project had to prove a real-HTTP permission ALLOW without a seeding fixture - the ALLOW path is now proven only at the unit level via FakeRolePermissionGateway; the real-HTTP ALLOW path for a genuine tenant grant remains undemonstrated end-to-end pending a narrow, production-real seeding fixture this project does not yet have (same disclosed InternalsVisibleTo wall as round 3, now with no safe shortcut around it).

Verified: dotnet build clean. 62/62 feature unit tests (was 61, +2/-1 net). 207/207 integration tests (re-pointed four tests; one unrelated, pre-existing ObservabilityTests failure reproduced once in a 207-test run, passed cleanly both in isolation and on a full-suite re-run - confirmed a flake, not a regression from this fix). 200/200 unit tests, no regression. 64/64 structural checks (was 59, +5 new ZB-07 checks, 1 repointed to the renamed AC03 test name). Module-reference/traceability/secret-scan/vulnerability-audit all still PASS.
